note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits.

problems.original_statement: Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations nonetheless default to cause-specific hazards or censor competing events without matching the estimator to the causal question, and recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly. The step where an analyst censors follow-up at death is an identifying decision that selects among these estimands, and it is normally executed silently inside data preparation, where no reviewer sees it as a decision at all.
problems.correction_note: Censoring at a competing event does not select or identify an estimand. It changes the observed-data analysis, and it supports a hypothetical elimination estimand only when that intervention is well defined and its identification conditions hold. Calling the censoring step the choice of estimand was the wrong description of what it does.
problems.statement: Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations default to cause-specific hazards or to censoring at the competing event. Censoring does not select among those estimands: it alters the observed-data analysis, and it corresponds to a hypothetical elimination of the competing event only when that intervention is well defined and its identification conditions hold, which is a claim the analysis has to make and defend. Estimators for competing events inside emulated trials exist and are being applied. Off-the-shelf support for joint recurrent-event and terminal-event contrasts under sustained strategies remains limited, and no reporting standard requires the censoring decision to be justified as an identifying assumption rather than executed inside data preparation.
problems.why_open: The estimands differ in what they assume rather than in what they fit, so a wrong choice produces a well-behaved analysis of the wrong quantity and nothing downstream flags it. Separable effects require decomposing a treatment into components with separately meaningful effects, which is a substantive claim about the drug that most applied settings cannot support. The combination of recurrent and terminal events with sustained-strategy emulation is not worked out in available software, so an analyst who chooses correctly on competing risks may have no estimator for the regime they wanted.
problems.proposed_direction: Prespecify the estimand as a cumulative incidence, a restricted mean event-free time or a recurrent-event contrast, and name the intercurrent-event strategy for each competing event in the protocol. Require that any censoring at a competing event be justified as an identifying assumption, with the intervention it corresponds to stated and its conditions argued, which turns a data-cleaning line into a reviewable claim. Compare multistate g-computation, joint frailty models, separable effects and recurrent-event targeted learning on data generated with a known competing-event structure, and build the joint recurrent-and-terminal case for sustained strategies, which is the gap in available implementations.
